title: CLI Coding Agent Failure Taxonomy
description: A closed-set vocabulary for classifying outcomes of CLI coding agent tasks. Designed for evaluation harnesses, audit logs, and regression dashboards. Cross-referenced with NIST AI RMF (validity, robustness, privacy, fairness, security) and ISO/IEC 42001 governance concepts.

task_id.description: Stable identifier for the task whose outcome is being recorded. Should be unique within the harness run.

category.description: Closed set of failure categories. See spec section 'Categories' for definitions and NIST AI RMF mapping.

severity.description: Severity tier for triage. Does not affect whether the task is counted as failed.

details.description: Human-readable explanation. One sentence. Cite a concrete part of the agent's output or trace.

files_involved.description: Repository-relative paths the failure touched. Empty if the failure is not localised to specific files.

agent.description: Identifier of the CLI agent that produced the outcome (e.g. claude-code, codex, gemini-cli). Optional but recommended for cross-agent comparison.

model.description: Underlying model name plus version, if known. Optional.

trace_url.description: Pointer to a stored trace of the agent run. Optional. Recommended for audit-grade deployments.

timestamp.description: When the outcome was recorded. ISO 8601.

orientation_miss.description: Agent spent a disproportionate share of its turns on exploration without producing output. Typical operational signal: more than half of turns spent reading the codebase or asking clarifying questions.

scope_creep.description: Agent modified files outside the scope it was assigned (owned_files, allowed paths). The change may be technically correct but violates the operating contract.

test_regression.description: Agent broke at least one existing test that was passing before its run. Highest-priority failure category; usually a hard gate.

incomplete.description: Agent stopped before fulfilling the completion signals declared in the task brief. Often pairs with 'context_miss' but is logged separately because the remediation differs.

timeout.description: Agent hit its wall-clock or max-turns budget. Distinct from 'incomplete': the agent might have finished given more budget; with 'incomplete' it would not.

conflict.description: Agent's changes collide with a concurrent agent's changes in a way that requires reconciliation. Specific to multi-agent orchestration.

context_miss.description: Agent had everything it needed to operate (budget, scope) but lacked the contextual knowledge to complete the task. Often signals a documentation gap rather than an agent defect.

hallucination.description: Agent produced output that references APIs, files, or facts that do not exist in the codebase or its dependencies. Includes uncompilable code and fabricated identifiers.

$defs.priority_order_note: When more than one category applies, the classifier assigns the one nearest the top of this list. The order reflects severity for downstream gating, not statistical frequency.

examples.details: Agent removed the null check in `process_input` to satisfy a different test; existing test 'test_handles_null_input' now fails.
Agent reformatted three files outside owned_files; reformat was correct but unauthorised.
Agent imported `bernstein.core.does_not_exist`; module is absent from the installed package.
